subject: Biotechnology
title: DNA Data Storage
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on DNA Data Storage.

hook.text: All the world's data could fit in a room full of DNA — nature's storage medium outlasts any hard drive.

buildup.text: Binary data is converted to base sequences — four letters give DNA twice the information density of binary.

discovery.text: Researchers stored an entire movie, an operating system, and a $50 gift card in DNA — then read it back perfectly.

twist.text: Write speed is the bottleneck — DNA synthesis is a million times slower than writing to a hard drive.

climax.text: DNA lasts thousands of years in cool, dry conditions — woolly mammoth genomes survived 10,000 years in permafrost.

punchline.text: Write data in DNA — the oldest storage medium becomes the newest.

quiz.question: What is the biggest limitation of DNA data storage currently?
options: DNA degrades too quickly to store data long-term
Writing data to DNA is extremely slow compared to electronic storage
Only text can be stored in DNA, not images or video
